source_caption:
"The greatest trick the Devil ever pulled was convincing the world he didn't exist."

The Usual Suspects concludes with a legendary twist where the physically disabled, timid con artist Verbal Kint (Kevin Spacey) walks away from a police interrogation, shedding his limp to reveal he is the mythical crime lord Keyser Söze. The entire story he narrated was fabricated, utilizing details from objects in the interrogation room of police station. As he walks away and that limp slowly disappears, we realize that every single detail the names, the places, the motives was being improvised in real-time right in front of the detective's eyes. It’s the ultimate human "blind spot." We see what we expect to see, and by the time the coffee cup hits the floor, the truth has already vanished into thin air.
